groups.contract: Negotiated navigation retains authoritative GET rendering and bounded redirect handling
groups.disposition: Both complete 762-line bodies personally read; actual textual comparison has no differences. POST redirect handling follows at most five local redirects, propagates updated cookies into each internal GET, preserves all Set-Cookie response values, and switches to hard navigation at strategic boundaries or an unresolved redirect limit. Malformed local URI and unsuccessful or non-root internal render have explicit fallback/error responses. Cookie removal and replacement are parsed before constructing a new valid HeaderValue. No assumed transaction rollback for the already completed POST. Tests were read, not executed. URL/HeaderValue conversion expectations depend on the actual admitted URI/header grammar; no reachable invalid header counterexample is established.

groups.contract: Fragment extraction has an explicit body budget but incomplete error semantics remain qualified
groups.disposition: Root extraction uses a 16 MiB to_bytes budget. Invalid UTF-8 or missing markers returns the original collected document; ASCII marker boundaries preserve valid UTF-8 slicing. Successful extraction removes Content-Length before changing the body. Collection failure returns an empty body with the original response parts, potentially retaining a success status and prior length metadata. This is a source-backed error-path contract question, not an accepted ordinary route failure: no reachable oversized/erroring successful page or downstream client consequence was personally established. Acceptance requires the owning HTTP error policy and a concrete route/body witness before promotion; do not infer a runtime defect solely from the theoretical budget path.
